title: Seller micro-battle lab: quick deck + battlecard (draft)
content:
Purpose / intent:
- Build a compact 8-slide deck + two-sided battlecard that an SE/AE can carry into a 20–25 minute pilot kickoff or technical qualification.
- Focus: fast qualification, clear fallback economics, concrete pilot asks, and a 3-step canary that engineers can run with minimal ops support.

Quick TL;DR for slide 1 (elevator):
- 30s seller script: ‘Redwood lets you run production LLM features with predictable latency & cost across hosted, reserved, and private modes. For pilots we recommend a latency-first canary with auto-fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant — keeps UX tight while protecting spend.’

Target personas / call picks:
- Integration Architect / Platform Engineer: cares about latency SLOs, rollout policies, and private deployment options.
- Product Manager (AI feature owner): cares about user experience and cost per session.
- SRE / Infra contact: wants canary/runbook and rollback guardrails.

Slide deck outline (compact 8 slides):
1) Headline + 30s script + use-case one-liner (search assist, summarization, chat persist).
2) Architecture sketch (client -> Redwood API -> routing policy -> model variants) — highlight fallback path. (Speaker note: keep diagram minimal; call out region routing & dedicated pool option.)
3) Pilot plan (3-step): quick smoke (5k tokens/day), latency canary (2 hours), scale test (24–72h).
4) Fallback economics (numbers): sample token pricing delta (hosted v quantized dedicated), expected cost per 1k requests, margin if caching used. (Add small table.)
5) Quality guardrails: eval prompts to run pre/post, acceptable drop thresholds, rollback triggers.
6) Operations checklist: token/key rotation, observability hooks (console routes), tracing tag suggestion.
7) Negotiation asks: needed logs/retention, SLA expectations, reserved capacity options.
8) Next steps & playbook: who to loop (SE, Solutions Eng, SRE), pilot kickoff checklist, scheduled canary window.

Battlecard (one page cheat-sheet to hand sellers):
- Top objection: ‘Your latency claim sounds theoretical — how do we know it holds at our scale?’
  - Quick answer: share Redwood-verified perf bench for similar seq lengths + propose 2-hour latency canary on a dedicated pool with SLOs instrumented in the Console.
  - Proof points: internal bench id INF-2178, past customer case study (internal link).

- Top objection: ‘We can host this ourselves / cheaper on cloud GPUs.’
  - Quick answer: compare total cost of ownership vs per-token economics; highlight time-to-production, routing/fallback logic, and observability (time & people savings). Offer a short TCO sketch during pilot.

- Top objection: ‘We can't expose data to hosted API.’
  - Quick answer: Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) + key management & audit trails. Suggest private pilot with redwood private control plane; propose NDAs + SOC artifacts.

- Risk card: model drift / quality regression
  - Mitigation: tie regression alerts to prompt sets, run weekly evals, automated rollback to previous model variant. Suggest initial guard: 2% F1 drop -> trigger rollback.

Pilot checklist (practical ops):
- Access: API key + pilot project created in Console (owner: SE).
- Observability: set up route-level latency & cost charts; enable tracing for sample sessions.
- Fallbacks: register a quantized fallback variant and a regional fallback. Validate auto-switch in staging.
- Data handling: confirm log retention and PII redaction policy; confirm KMS integration.
- Metrics: define success metrics (p95 latency <= target, cost per session <= $X, user success rate >= Y).

Speaker notes / seller cues (bite-sized):
- ‘If they push back on price, ask about expected QPS and session length. We can estimate unit economics in 5 mins.’
- ‘If they ask about model parity, propose a run with identical prompt set for 48h to compare.’
- ‘If ops worry about incident blast radius, propose canary with traffic shadowing and an escape hatch to dedicated pool.’

Open questions / TODOs (for internal review):
- Fill the sample cost table with up-to-date per-token numbers (ask pricing ops).
- Add a one-paragraph customer proof (small anonymized case study) — reach out to account team.
- Confirm the default rollback threshold with ML leads (Priya).
- Create a one-page printable battlecard (PDF) after this draft is stable.

Quick links / refs: 
- Confluence: field-kit: /display/GO/Inference+Field+Kit (placeholder) -> link in linked_artifacts
- JIRA: INF-2178 (latency bench), SE-302 (pilot template)
- GH: field-assets/pull/89 (sample dashboard json)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep language in slides >90% benefit-led; avoid infra jargon unless SE is present.
- Make fallback economics visual (bar chart with three columns: hosted, dedicated quantized, private on-prem) — ops can fill exact values.
- Consider two versions: one for platform-engineer-heavy accounts (more slides) and one ultra-compact 3-slide hack for SDRs.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Liam to draft slide 4 (cost table) by Tue.
- Priya to confirm rollback threshold and put a short note on model drift protocol by Wed.
- I (Maya) to put this copy into slides and share in #go-to-market for comments by Fri.

Rough speaker one-liners to copy into notes: 
- ‘We recommend starting small and validating latency — if performance looks good, scale in 24–72h.’
- ‘Fallbacks are not a downgrade; they are an insurance policy to keep UX consistent while we tune models and caching.’

End of draft.
